observed_behaviors: Saving requires observation-form permission and a valid CSRF token.
With no observation ID, the controller starts from a new observation template; it binds form, active patient, encounter, user, provider group, and authorization context before validation.
The controller validates the observation and saves the main record and sub-observations inside an explicit transaction with rollback on failure.

Persistence generates a UUID, creates and links an encounter form when form_id is absent, defaults an unqualified code to LOINC, inserts a new form_observation row when no record ID exists, and reloads the persisted record.
Sub-observations inherit the saved parent ID, patient, encounter, and form ID.
gaps: The same service updates an existing observation row in place, so this locator is not eligible as an amendment/version-history comparator.
A durable success audit event is not established; the inspected service contains a TODO for save-event dispatch.
Row locking, idempotency, replay behavior, approved-Site scope, and retry recovery are not established.
The source identifies portions of the observation implementation as AI-generated; no runtime or maturity inference is made.

observed_behaviors: OpenMRS defines an observation as a single unit of clinical information and explicitly warns against altering the official encounter record in place.
Saving an existing observation requires a change message and edit-observation privilege.

A dirty existing observation is copied without its original ID, saved as a new row, linked through previousVersion, and the original observation is voided with the change message for historical retention.
When the original status is FINAL, the replacement status becomes AMENDED.
The observation model exposes PRELIMINARY, FINAL, and AMENDED states and describes the previous-version relationship explicitly.
gaps: No user-facing amendment confirmation, reviewer approval, signature, or reason-quality validation was established.
Concurrency locking and idempotent amendment replay are not established.
Approved-Site scope and minimum-necessary disclosure are not established.
For complex observations, the inspected service may purge the previous complex payload; complete binary-history preservation requires separate verification.
The model is audited, but the exact durable audit reader and end-user provenance display were not inspected.

observed_behaviors: The new/edit action derives patient and encounter from the active session, resolves the requested form or observation, and uses a default empty observation template when no record resolves.
Single-record lookup is constrained by observation ID and patient ID and can populate child observations.
The list action filters by active patient, active encounter, form ID, and absence of a parent-observation ID so only top-level records seed the result.
Encounter retrieval filters by patient and encounter, orders top-level observations newest first, and attaches each record's sub-observations.
Hierarchy population identifies top-level results and attaches child records using parent_observation_id.
gaps: The inspected hierarchy population establishes parent and immediate-child behavior; arbitrary multi-level hierarchy is not established.
form_id and a default empty observation template do not establish a configurable care-plan or clinical-template hierarchy.
Approved-Site filtering is not established.
Single-record lookup is patient-scoped but does not itself include encounter scope.
Authorization beyond the controller's observation-form permission and privacy behavior outside the active patient context remain unknown.

observed_behaviors: Incident detail exposes reported, under_investigation, pending_review, closed, and reopened statuses in desktop and mobile selectors, and selection auto-submits.
A visible review-progress checklist covers incident details, people and injuries, reconstructed timeline, contributing factors, root cause or 5-Whys, preventative steps, and closure.

gaps: The checklist and pending_review state do not gate closure in the inspected closure action.

This is source evidence from a repository described as pre-launch; no runtime, maturity, or production credit is available.

eligibility.reason: BeaconHS provides a direct H&S incident object with an exact pending-review status, investigation artifacts, and visible review checklist. It does not establish an enforced review gate.

observed_behaviors: Closure requires the distinct incidents.close capability and an owner/site-aware record-visibility guard.
The incident row is locked before the closure mutation.
Closing sets closedAt, clears inProgress, locks the incident, and records a transactional domain event for downstream notification, integration, and flow consumers.
The action subsequently records activity audit information and refreshes incident detail and list views.
Closed incidents display the closure date, appear locked, and expose status and audit history in Activity.
gaps: Review checklist completion, pending flow gates, and corrective-action state do not gate closure; the inspected action permits a direct status change to closed.
No closure confirmation, rationale, approval, signature, reviewer identity, or effectiveness decision is required.
The schema has closedByTenantUserId, but the inspected closure mutation does not populate it.
Activity audit recording occurs after the closure transaction, so atomic closure-plus-audit recovery is not established.
Selecting a non-closed status clears closedAt and unlocks the incident; a user with update permission can also unlock a closed incident separately, so closure immutability is not established.

bounded_search.reason: Direct incident closure status and actor/timestamp timeline, but no close-specific authority or mandatory evidence gate.
Closure is state-gated and records actor/time, but the object is a deviation and its linked CAPA may remain open.
Calculator library, not an incident-closure workflow.
